findings.evidence: network.json shows GET http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/admin/fiscal/z-report -> status 422 (Unprocessable Content). Console.json captures matching error: level=error, text='Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 422 (Unprocessable Content)', url='/api/admin/fiscal/z-report', ts=1779300400685. DOM of state 02 contains NO [role=alert], NO .toast, NO .alert-* visible to the caissier. The error is silent — fiscal Z-report status indicator (top-bar lock icon) just renders neutrally. This is a NF525-fiscal-surface 4xx with zero user feedback. P0 per REVIEWER_PROTOCOL #6 silent_error. Reproduced in console.json of state 02 and state 05 (same admin shell mount).
findings.expected: Either /api/admin/fiscal/z-report should return 200/204 (no Z pending = valid state, not validation error) OR if 422 is semantically correct, a [role=alert] / status pill MUST appear so the caissier knows fiscal state is anomalous
findings.actual: 422 fires on every admin-shell mount; no UI surfaces it
findings.fix_hint: app/Http/Controllers/Admin/FiscalZReportController.php (or wherever GET /api/admin/fiscal/z-report is routed): if no Z pending close, return 200 {status:'no_pending'} not 422. Alternatively wire the admin shell's fiscal indicator to display a 'fiscal: unknown' badge when 4xx occurs.
findings.fix_proposal: Backend: replace 422 response in GET z-report with a 200 payload describing state (no pending close), OR add a frontend error handler in admin shell mount that surfaces fiscal-fetch failures via the alert system.

findings.evidence: Sidebar of admin shell visibly renders RAW i18n keys 'MENU.COMMUNICATIONS', 'MENU.USERS', 'MENU.ACCOUNTS' as section headers in state 13 PNG (uppercased by CSS text-transform). DOM grep returns lowercase 'menu.communications', 'menu.users', 'menu.accounts', 'menu.reports', 'menu.setup' as visible labels. Console.json of every navigation state (02, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17) contains 10+ '[intlify] Not found 'menu.communications'/'menu.users'/'menu.accounts'/'menu.reports'/'menu.setup' key in 'fr' locale messages.' warnings each. These render to the caissier on the Suivi page — visible defect. Regex match per REVIEWER_PROTOCOL #1: ^[a-z]+\.[a-z_]+$.
findings.fix_hint: resources/lang/fr.json — add keys menu.communications / menu.users / menu.accounts / menu.reports / menu.setup. Confirmed missing via [intlify] warning at app.js:137486 (sidebar component group-label resolver).
findings.fix_proposal: Add the 5 missing keys to resources/lang/fr.json (and en.json for parity).

findings.evidence: console.json of state 17 captures multiple 'pageerror' entries: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading \'emitsOptions\')' originating at /js/app.js (NOT vendor.js / NOT pusher). Stack: shouldUpdateComponent -> updateComponent -> processComponent -> patch, fires under <PosComponent onVnodeUnmounted> and <PaymentComponent props={form:Object}>. Fires 5+ times during navigation from POS to Suivi commandes (between state 16 confirm and state 17 capture). This is a Vue lifecycle bug: PaymentComponent emits a re-render after parent vnode is null. Not in vendor allowlist.
findings.fix_hint: resources/js/components/admin/pos/PaymentComponent.vue or PosComponent.vue — guard emit calls in onVnodeUnmounted hook with `if (instance && instance.proxy)` before emitting. Frozen-zone PaymentComponent.vue is involved; if root cause is there, gate-locked LOCK doc required. Alternative: PosComponent.vue parent passing null prop to PaymentComponent during teardown — fix at the parent side outside frozen zone.
findings.fix_proposal: Investigate PosComponent.vue parent unmount sequence; guard PaymentComponent props prior to teardown. Likely fixable outside frozen zone in PosComponent.vue.

findings.evidence: console.json of state 16 captures pageerror: 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading \'id\')' originating at vendor.js:6487:9126 (Array.reduce) called via wrappedFn at app.js:14946 — invoked from <VueSelect id="customer" modelValue=12 ...> during delivery customer injection. The customer modelValue=12 is set programmatically (capture observation 'delivery injection ok=true uid=42 custId=12') but VueSelect's option-reduce step finds an undefined entry in the options array and crashes. The delivery flow visibly succeeded (state 16 PNG shows name/phone/address populated), but the underlying error is logged and could break in production where injection is via UI search (not DOM injection).
findings.expected: VueSelect customer dropdown should accept modelValue=12 without crashing on options.reduce
findings.actual: Pageerror fires during state 16 customer set
findings.fix_hint: vendor.js code is third-party VueSelect, but the consumer (POS delivery form) is passing an options array that contains undefined entries. Inspect resources/js/components/admin/pos/PosCustomerSelect.vue (or wherever the customer VueSelect lives) — filter options for falsy/undefined before passing to VueSelect. Likely root: customer list contains a deleted/soft-deleted customer surfaced as undefined.
findings.fix_proposal: Add `.filter(c => c && c.id)` to the customer options array before VueSelect bind.

findings.evidence: Capture-time PLAN section 5 specifies state 02='Open cash drawer modal with 50€ initial — submitted', states 03/04 = drawer dialog open/submitted. PNG states 03 + 04 show 'SESSION ACTIVE' modal with 'CAISSE OUVERTE LE 20/05 13:31', opening_amount_text='100,00 €' (not 50€), and 'MONTANT ACTUEL 100,00 €'. The drawer was already open before this audit began. capture-time JSON observation confirms: 'state3: overlay_visible=true, open_form_present=false, opening_amount_text="100,00 €"'. State 04 PNG is byte-identical to state 03 (same modal, same 100€) — no transition occurred. The drawer-open scenario REQUIRED by Wave A plan was SKIPPED because the session was pre-existing. This breaks audit integrity: the GStack capture team did not exercise the scenario the PLAN demanded. A future cold-environment run might fail (no auto-open path tested here).
findings.expected: State 03 = empty drawer-open form (100€/50€ input field); state 04 = post-submit confirmation that drawer just opened
findings.actual: Both states show pre-existing Session Active modal (drawer opened 4.5 hours earlier at 13:31)
findings.fix_hint: tests/e2e/test-e2e-wave-t-caisse-to-delivered-A-pos.spec.js — add a preflight step: call POST /api/admin/cash-session/close-current (or DELETE current session) before opening drawer, OR adapt the spec to detect Session Active and skip cleanly with a flag (e.g. fixture.drawer_was_pre_open=true). Pre-flight check #6 in PLAN should include `php artisan tinker --execute='App\Models\CashDrawerSession::where("status","open")->update(["status"=>"closed"]);'`
findings.fix_proposal: Add preflight that ensures no active cash session before Wave A boot, OR document state 02/03/04 semantics for the case where drawer was already open.

findings.evidence: State 10 PNG shows toast 'Article ajouté au panier' (green checkmark, top-right) STILL visible after mode 'À emporter' is selected. DOM confirms: 'Article ajouté au panier' present in 10-pos-takeaway-mode-selected.dom.html. The toast is sticky / not auto-dismissed before the mode change. Visually clutters the UX as the caissier moves to mode selection. Per REVIEWER_PROTOCOL #5/8: toast cluttering = UX-quality P2.
findings.expected: Toast auto-dismisses within 3s or upon next user action (mode select)
findings.actual: Toast persists during mode select and into state 11 capture window
findings.fix_hint: resources/js/utils/toast.js or wherever vue-toast configures duration — set timeout=2500ms (currently appears unbounded for some events). Or in the cart 'item added' emitter, programmatically dismiss prior toasts on next action.
findings.fix_proposal: Reduce toast duration to 2.5s or dismiss on user action.

findings.evidence: State 09 PNG: cart panel right side displays a SINGLE visible line 'Sandwich Cayenne 7.00€' even though DOM contains 3 lines (Sandwich Cayenne, Tacos, Coca-Cola 33cl). Total shown is 17.00€ (correct sum). The cart container does not scroll-into-view its content; the 2 lines below the fold are clipped. Capture observation 'line_count:3, line_names:[Sandwich Cayenne, Tacos, Coca-Cola 33cl]' confirms data exists. State 11 (payment modal) covers the cart so the cashier may never see lines 2-3 before confirming. UX risk: caissier confirms an order without visually verifying all lines.
findings.expected: Cart panel either auto-scrolls so latest line is visible OR shows a compact list (3 lines at glance for short orders)
findings.actual: Cart shows 1 line, 2 lines below fold not visible
findings.fix_hint: resources/js/components/admin/pos/PosCartComponent.vue or similar — add `el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight` on item-add, OR set min-height so 3-4 lines render without scroll.
findings.fix_proposal: Auto-scroll cart to bottom on item add; min-height for small carts.

findings.evidence: Capture-time observation: 'state12: order1Id=69 api_total=NaN'. Same for state17 order2: 'api_total=NaN'. Fixture file documents 'cart_modal_total_match: false' for BOTH orders. While numeric integrity HOLDS across visible surfaces (17,00€ in cart == 17,00€ in modal == 17,00€ in receipt == 17,00€ in tracker, verified via PNG inspect + DOM grep), the spec's own parse-receipt-api-response logic returns NaN for the total. This indicates the receipt API payload does not expose a top-level `total` field — instead probably nested as `data.total_amount_price` or similar. The fact that the GStack spec recorded `false` on cart_modal_total_match WITHOUT raising a hard failure is itself an audit_integrity weak signal. Owner reading the fixture would conclude 'mismatch detected' — false alarm or symptom of real bug, the spec doesn't disambiguate.
findings.expected: Spec parses API total correctly; cart_modal_total_match: true OR explicit reason
findings.fix_hint: tests/e2e/test-e2e-wave-t-caisse-to-delivered-A-pos.spec.js — fix the API response parser to read `response.data.total_amount_price_in_cents` (or whichever NF525 field actually exists) instead of `response.total`. Then re-evaluate cart_modal_total_match.
findings.fix_proposal: Spec author: refactor api_total extraction; document the field path; set cart_modal_total_match true when source-of-truth fields agree.

findings.evidence: PLAN section 5 expects state 17 = 'Navigate to /admin/pos-orders-tracker; both orders visible in EN PRÉPARATION column'. State 17 PNG shows BOTH orders in EN PRÉPARATION (✓), correct. HOWEVER capture observation for state 17 contains 'state17: re-inject (DOM-anchored) ok=true reason=n/a uid=42' followed by 'state17 paymentForce: {ok:true, paymentMode:"card", selectedTerminalId:1, cardInput_filled:"1234"}'. The spec PROGRAMMATICALLY INJECTED the delivery customer (state 16) AND PROGRAMMATICALLY FORCED the payment mode + card input (state 17 pre-click). This means the audit did NOT exercise the natural UI flow for order #2 (livraison/TPE) — it patched Vue state via DOM injection. Owner mandate (PLAN §1) says 'every state captured visually + technically'. By injecting state, the GStack team bypassed potential UI bugs (e.g., the customer modal might fail in a real caissier session). This is audit_integrity P1 — Wave A's Order #2 path is not really tested end-to-end by UI clicks.
findings.expected: Order #2 customer + payment data entered via UI clicks (matching real caissier flow)
findings.actual: DOM-anchored state injection (custId=12, addrId=8, paymentMode='card' force-set)
findings.fix_hint: tests/e2e/test-e2e-wave-t-caisse-to-delivered-A-pos.spec.js — replace DOM injection with real UI click sequence on the delivery customer modal: type customer name, select from autocomplete, fill phone, fill address. Same for payment: click TPE tab, type card last-4, click confirm. If the UI itself prevents this (autocomplete server-side), THAT's a separate UI bug to file.
findings.fix_proposal: Replace DOM injection of order #2 customer+payment with click-driven flow; if UI prevents that, file a UX bug for the inability to complete delivery + TPE via clicks alone.

findings.evidence: Wave S-2 hook B-S2-BADGE specifies: 'Order #1 (cash) MUST show .cash-pending-badge element visible. Order #2 (TPE) MUST NOT show that badge.' Per Wave A PLAN A-S4 hook, cash-pending badge applies to Suivi tracker too. Capture observation for state 13: 'order1_cash_badge_present:false'. State 17 observation: 'order1_cash_badge:false, order2_cash_badge:false'. Order #1 paid CASH but `cash_badge_present=false` — Wave S-2 cash-pending badge requirement is NOT satisfied for the Suivi tracker. (PLAN may only require this for KDS, but the Suivi tracker is the same surface owner-facing; consistency expected.) NOTE: cash-pending semantics may apply only to UNPAID cash orders; Order #1 was already PAID at state 12 confirm, so 'cash-pending' may not apply post-pay. Still flagging because the capture team's badge check returned false on a cash-paid order — needs human verification whether badge should show on PAID-CASH-prepared or only PRE-PAY-CASH orders.
findings.expected: Either cash-pending badge present on Order #1 OR explicit spec stating the badge only applies pre-pay (in which case A-S4 hook on Suivi tracker is irrelevant for paid orders)
findings.actual: Both orders have cash_badge=false; spec ambiguous on semantics
findings.fix_hint: Document Wave S-2 badge semantics. Suspected: badge only on confirmed-but-unpaid cash orders waiting at the À ENCAISSER lane. If so, the Wave A PLAN A-S4 hook is correctly null (no À ENCAISSER orders this run). But the PLAN should be updated to state this explicitly to avoid future false-positive findings.
findings.fix_proposal: Clarify cash-pending-badge semantics in PLAN.md and in PosOrdersTrackerComponent.vue.
